hints: Use a shared trie so common pattern prefixes are processed once.
Count visits to automaton states while scanning the text.
Push counts along failure links in reverse breadth-first order.
analogy: Each position deposits a token at its longest matching prefix; failure links pass the token to shorter suffix matches.
example: In ababa, aba occurs twice and bab occurs once, including overlapping occurrences.
algorithm: Build the Aho-Corasick automaton for all patterns. Scan the text and increment the reached state at every position. Process states in reverse breadth-first order, adding each count to its failure parent. Output the count at each pattern's terminal state.
correctness: A pattern ends at a position exactly when its terminal node is the current state or a failure ancestor. Reverse propagation adds precisely one contribution for every such position, including overlaps.
complexity: For text length n and total pattern length L over 26 letters, O(n+26L) time and O(26L) space.
